task.title: Review draft sales-coaching notes
task.prompt: Independently challenge these draft coaching notes against the timestamped observations. Flag unsupported claims about emotions or intentions, wrong speaker attribution, missed client questions, and alternative explanations for each cue. Do not infer feelings.

evidence.content: The salesperson (S1) spoke 80% of the speaking time in this recording (busiest 2-minute stretch shown). Other explanations: The call may have been a planned presentation or demo.
The client in this call (S2) asked a question (from the transcript).

The salesperson (S1) started speaking while the client in this call (S2) was speaking (0.4 s of overlap); the client in this call (S2) stopped 0.4 s later. Other explanations: The client in this call (S2) may have been finishing anyway; Line delay can make turn-taking look like overlap.

The salesperson (S1) spoke faster than usual in this turn: about 6.9 vs a median of 4.4 estimated syllables/s. Uncertainty: syllable estimates are approximate (+/- ~15%) and depend on audio quality. Other explanations: Reading a list or numbers; Summarising familiar material.

3.2 s of silence after the salesperson (S1) finished before the client in this call (S2) spoke. Other explanations: Thinking or reading; Checking something off-call; A connection delay; Muted microphone.
The client in this call (S2) asked a question (from the transcript).
The salesperson (S1) spoke for 51 s without the other person taking a turn. Other explanations: The other person asked for a full explanation; A requested demo.

Audible breathing/sigh detected from the client in this call (S2) (score 0.90). Uncertainty: breathing is a weak detector class; replay to confirm. Other explanations: Microphone close to the mouth; Movement or walking; Detector false alarm on noise.
